methodological_rigor.justification: Comparative dosimetric study of two IGRT strategies in pediatric TBI: 34 children (21 FBCT, 13 CBCT) treated with identical field setups across two institutions. Retrospective dose recalculation using planning CT and pre-treatment IGRT images (FBCT or CBCT). Dosimetric metrics: PTV V90%/V100%/V110%, homogeneity index (HI), conformity index (CI), mean lung/kidney doses. Statistical analysis: Wilcoxon rank sum test comparing groups (p<0.05 significance). Well-balanced baseline characteristics. However, small sample size, retrospective design, no randomization, no assessment of clinical outcomes (radiation pneumonitis not statistically analyzed despite mention).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Comparative observational cohort (LoE 2b) in pediatric ALL/AML/AA patients undergoing curative TBI before hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Directly relevant clinical question: optimal IGRT guidance for multi-isocenter pediatric TBI. FBCT-guided approach shows superiority: better PTV coverage (V100% 92.81% vs. 90.40% in 12 Gy/6F; 93.97% vs. 91.44% in 3 Gy/1F), reduced lung/kidney doses. Findings inform institutional practice but limited by single comparison of two technologies.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods clearly describe patient selection, radiotherapy planning (identical protocols across institutions), IGRT approaches (FBCT integrated vs. CBCT sequential), and dose recalculation methodology. Baseline characteristics presented (Table 1). Results presented separately for 12 Gy and 3 Gy regimens with detailed dosimetric metrics (Table 2-3). However, no formal reporting standard applied; some methodological details sparse (e.g., deformable registration parameters in Velocity software); no data sharing statement; limited supplementary information.

novelty_literature.justification: First direct comparison of FBCT-based integrated multi-isocenter guidance versus CBCT-based sequential guidance in pediatric TBI. Both are established techniques but comparison novel in this population. Findings demonstrate FBCT superiority for target coverage and organ sparing in both myeloablative (12 Gy) and low-dose (3 Gy) regimens. Incremental contribution to IGRT methodology literature but addresses important clinical question.

writing_presentation.justification: Clear introduction contextualizing TBI evolution from 2D to multi-isocenter IMRT/VMAT and IGRT challenges. Methods comprehensively describe radiotherapy planning, patient selection, and distinct IGRT workflows (FBCT vs. CBCT). Results logically presented by regimen with detailed dosimetric comparisons. Discussion appropriately explains mechanisms (integrated vs. sequential registration) and places findings in clinical context. Strengths/limitations explicitly discussed.

key_strengths: First comparative dosimetric study of FBCT-based integrated guidance versus CBCT-based sequential guidance in pediatric multi-isocenter TBI
Consistent FBCT superiority across both regimens: 12 Gy/6F improved V100% from 90.40% to 92.81%, V110% decreased from 20.73% to 16.67% (all p<0.01); similar improvements in 3 Gy/1F regimen
Clinically meaningful organ sparing: mean lung dose reduction 0.14 Gy (12 Gy regimen) and 0.09 Gy (3 Gy regimen); mean kidney dose reduction 0.14 Gy and 0.02-0.03 Gy respectively

Mechanistic explanation: FBCT captures full-body geometry in single scan enabling simultaneous multi-isocenter alignment, whereas CBCT sequential approach risks inter-isocenter misalignment with cumulative setup errors
Well-controlled study design: identical field setups across institutions, same treatment planning team ensuring consistency
key_concerns: Small sample size (n=34, 21 FBCT vs. 13 CBCT) limits statistical power; no formal sample size calculation provided
Retrospective design without randomization: potential for allocation bias based on institutional equipment/preference rather than clinical indication
No assessment of clinical outcomes: study focuses on dosimetry without evaluating radiation pneumonitis, kidney toxicity, or survival differences despite discussing biological significance

Limited generalizability: pediatric population only; two institutions using specific equipment (Shanghai: uRT-linac 506c with FBCT; Fujian: Varian TrueBeam); findings may not apply to other FBCT/CBCT systems

Dose recalculation methodology differs between institutions (direct dose calculation vs. deformable registration and Velocity software), potentially introducing systematic differences independent of FBCT/CBCT guidance
Missing data on implementation: patient comfort, treatment time, total imaging dose not systematically compared
chief_reviewer.rationale: Well-executed comparative dosimetric study addressing clinically important IGRT question in pediatric TBI, with consistent demonstration of FBCT superiority. LoE 2b appropriate for observational comparative study. Tier 3 (competent comparative work with clear clinical relevance). Minor revisions recommended: prospective clinical outcome validation, formal sample size justification, standardized dose recalculation across institutions.
